text: The three days of travel in Genesis 22 lead one to read them as a kind of suspended sentence. Outwardly nothing happens; in truth everything of consequence is happening. The servants, the wood, the knife, and the fire are brought into marked notice, so that the instruments of the act are named before the act itself occurs. In the story obedience and horror are present together, and neither prevails. Faith is no feeling here; it is ordered in fixed relations, like a geometry, in Genesis 22.
